mutators.name: Viral abroad
mutators.text: 60% of your users are on another continent from the first wave: every request they make crosses an ocean.
mutators.why: Distance is latency you cannot scale away. A CDN answers cacheable requests near the user, so far users stop paying the round trip.

mutators.name: Licence audit
mutators.text: Your SQL database vendor raises its price by 75%, and every SQL database you run costs that much more.
mutators.why: When the database is the expensive part, keep load off it: a cache in front of reads, or a store priced for the access pattern.

mutators.name: Read storm
mutators.text: Users browse far more than they post: reads ×1.5, writes halved.
mutators.why: A read-heavy system is won with caches and edge hits, not bigger databases.

mutators.name: Write-heavy
mutators.text: Everybody posts: writes ×3 from the first wave.
mutators.why: Replicas do not scale writes. Queues smooth the bursts, and shards split the write rate.

mutators.name: Flaky zone
mutators.text: Your cloud region has a bad year: an availability zone goes down on waves 3, 6 and 10.
mutators.why: Two of everything is not enough if both are in the same zone. Spread replicas so losing a zone loses capacity, not the service.

mutators.name: Lean seed round
mutators.text: The investors got cold feet: you start with 60% of the cash, but the bank pays twice the interest cap.
mutators.why: With little money, the first design has to be right-sized: buy capacity just ahead of demand, not years ahead.

mutators.name: Cache vendor trouble
mutators.text: Your managed cache keeps restarting: a cache stampede on waves 5, 6 and 7.
mutators.why: A cold cache sends every read to the database at once. Size the database for the misses, or warm and coalesce.
